findings.finding: At 3X and 5X: severe left ventricular hypertrophy with subendocardial ischemic lesions, myxomatous mitral valve thickening, mitral insufficiency murmurs, jet lesions, LVOT endocardial thickening, right atrial granulomatous lesion, decreased blood pressure, increased heart rate, subtle increase in VPCs

findings.finding: Heart murmurs (grade II-III/VI) in one 3X dog and two 5X dogs

findings.finding: Heart was the only organ with treatment-related gross or histopathologic findings
findings.quote: The heart was the only organ with treatment related findings on gross pathology or histopathology.

findings.finding: Lower mean systolic blood pressure in 5X group (117 vs 124 mmHg)

findings.finding: No clinical signs associated with cardiac pathology
findings.quote: None of the dogs had clinical signs associated with their cardiac pathology.

findings.finding: Non-dose-dependent: infrequent self-limiting diarrhea/vomiting, mild blood glucose changes, mild ALP and potassium increases, mild platelet decrease

indication.quote: Indications: For the control of atopic dermatitis in dogs weighing at least 4 lbs body weight.

dose_regimen.route: Oral (gelatin capsules); given fasted in the field study (1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal)
dose_regimen.frequency: Single daily dose for 30 days, then taper to every other day or two times a week
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Taper to the minimum frequency that maintains the desired therapeutic effect
dose_regimen.quote: The initial daily dose of ATOPICA is 5 mg/kg/day (3.3-6.7 mg/kg/day) as a single daily dose for 30 days. Following this initial daily treatment period, the dose of ATOPICA may be tapered by decreasing the frequency of dosing to every other day or two times a week until a minimum frequency is reached which will maintain the desired therapeutic effect.

dose_multiples: 1X (6.7 mg/kg/day maximum exposure; constant or tapered)
target_animal_safety.duration: 90 days, once daily orally in fasted dogs (taper groups reduced at Days 30 and 60)

findings.finding: At maximum recommended dose for 90 days: footpad callus-like lesions, red/swollen pinnae, gingival proliferation, hyperkeratosis, hair loss, salivation, vomiting, diarrhea
findings.quote: Oral administration of ATOPICA capsules at the maximum recommended dose, when administered for 90 days causes callus-like lesions on the footpads, red/swollen pinnae, mild to moderate gingival proliferation, hyperkeratotic areas on the integument, hair loss, salivation, vomiting and diarrhea/abnormal stools.

findings.finding: Signs lessen or resolve on tapering
findings.quote: These clinical signs either lessen in severity or resolve as the drug is tapered to a lower dose.

findings.finding: At 3X and 5X: increased ESR, hyperproteinemia, hyperglobulinemia, hypoalbuminemia, hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia
findings.quote: Increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate, hyperproteinemia, hyperglobulinemia, hypoalbuminemia, hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and hypomagnesemia were observed at three and five times the recommended dose.

findings.finding: Above maximum recommended dose: raised/verruciform skin lesions, popliteal lymph node enlargement, weight loss
findings.quote: When the drug was administered at higher than the maximum recommended dose, raised lesions, verruciform areas on the integument, popliteal lymph node enlargement, and weight loss were also seen.

findings.finding: Gingival proliferation first seen Day 45, dose-related progression
findings.quote: The gingival proliferation, which was first observed on Day 45, followed a dose-related pattern in its progression and severity during the last six weeks of the study.

findings.finding: 52-week study (1X, 3X, 9X): dose-dependent vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, swollen gums, papillomas, periodontitis, gingivitis; reversible
findings.quote: Cyclosporine administered at 1, 3, and 9 times the recommended dosage caused dose-dependent vomiting, diarrhea, weight loss, swollen gums, papilloma growths, periodontitis, and gingivitis.

indication.text: Prevention and treatment of acute vomiting in dogs
indication.quote: Indication(s): For the prevention and treatment of acute vomiting in dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: 1.0 mg/kg (0.45 mg/lb), i.e. 1.0 mL/10 kg of the 10 mg/mL solution
dose_regimen.quote: Administer CERENIA Injectable Solution subcutaneously at 1.0 mg/kg (0.45 mg/lb) equal to 1.0 mL/10 kg (1.0 mL/22 lb) of body weight once daily for up to 5 consecutive days.

pharmacokinetics.value: SC 1 mg/kg gives Tmax, Cmax and AUC0 to 24 not statistically different from oral 2 mg/kg (no numeric values reported)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Crossover in 12 Beagles (6 per group), sampling 0.5-24 h
pharmacokinetics.quote: No statistical differences in the time to achieve maximum plasma concentration (Tmax), in maximum concentration (Cmax), or in area under the plasma concentration curve (AUC0 to 24) were detected between maropitant administered subcutaneously at a dosage of 1 mg/kg or orally at 2 mg/kg.

target_animal_safety.duration: Once daily subcutaneously for 15 days (Days 0-14); recovery groups observed to Day 36

findings.finding: Well tolerated; all dogs gained weight
findings.quote: Maropitant injectable solution was well tolerated in all dogs.

findings.finding: Injection site lesions at necropsy: 1 dog at 1X, 4 dogs at 3X, 6 dogs at 5X
findings.quote: Injection site lesions were identified at necropsy in one dog at 1 mg/kg (1X), 4 dogs at 3 mg/kg (3X), and 6 dogs at 5 mg/kg (5X).

findings.finding: Injection site thickening in 6 dogs at 3X and 5 dogs at 5X
findings.quote: The other daily injection sites were found to be slightly thickened on 1 or more occasions in 6 dogs at 3 mg/kg (3X) and 5 dogs at 5 mg/kg (5X).

findings.finding: Prolonged APTT (67.5 s) in one 1X male dog, relationship undetermined
findings.quote: The activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) was prolonged (67.5 seconds, reference range 9-15 seconds) in one male dog in the 1 mg/kg group on Study Day 15.

findings.finding: Conclusion: well tolerated in 16-week-old dogs up to 5 mg/kg for 15 days
findings.quote: Maropitant injectable solution (10 mg/mL) was well tolerated when administered subcutaneously to healthy 16-week-old dogs for 15 days at up to 5 mg/kg.

findings.finding: Separate study in 8-week-old puppies: increased frequency/severity of bone marrow hypoplasia at elevated doses
findings.quote: in this study with 8 week old puppies there was an increased frequency and greater severity of bone marrow hypoplasia reported for dogs treated with elevated doses of maropitant.

findings.finding: Not supported for use in puppies 8-11 weeks of age
findings.quote: The results of this study do not support the safe use of CERENIA in puppies 8-11 weeks of age.

effectiveness.design: Multi-site (30 US clinics), randomized (1 placebo : 3 maropitant), masked, placebo-controlled field study in client-owned dogs presenting with acute vomiting; SC 1 mg/kg on Day 0 then SC (1 mg/kg) or oral (2 mg/kg) once daily as needed up to Day 4; 275 dogs enrolled (206 maropitant, 69 placebo)
